expo-milnor-clarity.evidence: H4/H5: L4 writes points of $\mathbb P(V)$ as classes $[\alpha]$ of differential forms and L11 defines $Z$ as a ratio of forms ($\alpha_H/\iota_\xi\alpha$) that is said (L25) to take values in a distribution — the objects being divided are never typed. L1 '$\mathbb P(V)$ the projective line object' is used before it is defined. H2: the classical picture (stereographic coordinate $z=z_1/z_0$ on $\mathbb{CP}^1$) is mentioned only as the last word.
expo-milnor-clarity.notes: Milnor H1-H8 = [2, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1] (T=8/16, fail); weakest: H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, H7, H8. Suggested rewrite (not applied; owner rule 'ask before changing'): Begin with the classical case: 'On $\mathbb{CP}^1$ the affine chart $\{z_0\ne0\}$ has coordinate $z=z_1/z_0$, stereographic projection from the pole.' Then give the categorical version with the type of $Z$ stated. Cite the definition of $\mathbb P(V)$. Audit doc: docs/audits/2026-10-10-milnor-voice-audit-ch1-ch2.md

trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Full read of the definition: Reeb splitting alpha = alpha_H + Theta wedge iota_xi alpha, the open set U_xi where iota_xi alpha != 0 (scale-invariant, so well defined on P(V)), the affine coordinate Z, and a tikzcd. Closer 'supply the stereographic projection intrinsically, without external coordinates' reads as standard mathematical usage (the appositive fixes what 'intrinsically' means) rather than manufactured negation-contrast; left unedited.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: Separate flag (not a trap): the tikzcd right-hand vertical arrow asserts P(V) is isomorphic to Omega^1_H(A); a projective line object being isomorphic to the full module of horizontal 1-forms looks wrong - worth checking whether the intended target is P(Omega^1_H(A)).
